facts.text: Ian Barry (director): Ian Barry is an Australian director of film and TV.
Michael Govan: Michael Govan( born 1963) is the director of the Los Angeles County Museum of Art since 2006.
Michael Govan: Prior to this, Govan worked as the director of the Dia Art Foundation in New York City.
Peter Levin: Peter Levin is an American director of film, television and theatre.
Gunasekhar: Gunasekar (born Gunasekar Karri; 2 June 1964) is an Indian film director and screenwriter known for his works exclusively in Telugu cinema.

Gunasekhar: Gunasekhar directed the Children's classic "Ramayanam" (1997), which won the National Film Award for Best Children's Film, including several state Nandi Awards for that year, and was screened at the International Children's Film Festival of India.
Gunasekhar: The 2003 action film, "Okkadu", which won eight state Nandi Awards, and four Filmfare Awards South including the Filmfare Award for Best Director – Telugu
Gunasekhar: , the blockbuster film became the highest grossing Telugu film for that year, and was remade into various Indian languages.
Gunasekhar: His latest venture is the historical film, Rudhramadevi which was released in October 2015 for wide positive reviews and became one of the biggest hits of the year.
Dana Blankstein: Dana Blankstein- Cohen( born March 3, 1981) is the director of the Israeli Academy of Film and Television.
Dana Blankstein: She is a film director, and an Israeli culture entrepreneur.
Olav Aaraas: Olav Aaraas( born 10 July 1950) is a Norwegian historian and museum director.
Olav Aaraas: He was born in Fredrikstad.

Olav Aaraas: From 1982 to 1993 he was the director of Sogn Folk Museum, from 1993 to 2010 he was the director of Maihaugen and from 2001 he has been the director of the Norwegian Museum of Cultural History.
Olav Aaraas: In 2010 he was decorated with the Royal Norwegian Order of St. Olav.
Etan Boritzer: Etan Boritzer( born 1950) is an American writer of children ’s literature who is best known for his book" What is God?" first published in 1989.

Etan Boritzer: His best selling" What is?" illustrated children's book series on character education and difficult subjects for children is a popular teaching guide for parents, teachers and child- life professionals.
Etan Boritzer: Boritzer gained national critical acclaim after" What is God?" was published in 1989 although the book has caused controversy from religious fundamentalists for its universalist views.
Etan Boritzer: The other current books in the" What is?" series include
Etan Boritzer: What is Love?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Death?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Beautiful?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Funny?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Right?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Peace?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Money?,
Etan Boritzer: What is Dreaming?,
Etan Boritzer: What is a Friend?,
Etan Boritzer: What is True?,
Etan Boritzer: What is a Family?,
Etan Boritzer: What is a Feeling?"
Etan Boritzer: The series is now also translated into 15 languages.

Etan Boritzer: Boritzer was first published in 1963 at the age of 13 when he wrote an essay in his English class at Wade Junior High School in the Bronx, New York on the assassination of John F. Kennedy.
Etan Boritzer: His essay was included in a special anthology by New York City public school children compiled and published by the New York City Department of Education.
Etan Boritzer: Boritzer now lives in Venice, California and maintains his publishing office there also.
Etan Boritzer: He has helped numerous other authors to get published through" How to Get Your Book Published!" programs.
Etan Boritzer: Boritzer is also a yoga teacher who teaches regular classes locally and guest- teaches nationally.
Etan Boritzer: He is also recognized nationally as an erudite speaker on" The Teachings of the Buddha."
John Farrell (businessman): John Farrell is the director of YouTube in Latin America.
Sainikudu: Sainikudu ("Soldier") is a 2006 Indian Telugu-language political action film written and directed by Gunasekhar.
Sainikudu: It stars Mahesh Babu and Trisha in the lead roles with Kamna Jethmalani in an item number and cameo appearance.
Sainikudu: Irrfan Khan is the main antagonist, and Prakash Raj, Kota Srinivasa Rao, Telangana Shakuntala, and Ajay play supporting roles.
Sainikudu: Harris Jayaraj scored the music.
Sainikudu: Balasubramaniam handled the camera work while Sreekar Prasad handled the editing.
Sainikudu: Sainikudu" was released on 16 November 2006, and the music was released on 21 October 2006.
John Donatich: John Donatich is the Director of Yale University Press.

Lothar Mendes: Lothar Mendes( 19 May 1894 – 24 February 1974) was a Jewish German- born screenwriter and film director. who began his career as an actor in Vienna and Berlin in Max Reinhardt's famous troupe.
Lothar Mendes: He went to America in the early 1920s and there he remained until 1933, directing more than a dozen features, mostly frothy comedies, while under contract to Paramount.
Lothar Mendes: His films included the last silent film made in America," The Four Feathers"( 1929) and the murder mystery" Payment Deferred"( 1933) starring British actor Charles Laughton.
The Kingdom of Twilight: The Kingdom of Twilight is a 1929 film directed by British author and explorer Alexander MacDonald.
The Laughing Lady: " For the 1929 film see The Laughing Lady( 1929 film)"
The Laughing Lady: The Laughing Lady is a 1946 British Technicolor musical drama film directed by Paul L. Stein and starring Anne Ziegler, Webster Booth and Francis L. Sullivan.
The Laughing Lady: Based on a play by Ingram D'Abbes, its plot follows a young aristocrat who makes a deal with Robespierre during the French Revolution.

Melancholie der Engel: Melancholie der Engel( English: The Angels' Melancholia) is a 2009 German independent experimental art film directed, shot, and edited by Marian Dora and cowritten by Dora and Carsten Frank( under the pseudonym Frank Oliver, used due to artistic disagreements).
Melancholie der Engel: It was planned since 2003 though the shooting was delayed due to monetary issues.
Melancholie der Engel: It premiered at Weekend of Fear Festival in Erlangen and Nuremberg, Middle Franconia, Franconia, Bavaria, Germany, on 1 May 2009.

Melancholie der Engel: It was also screened at the New York International Independent Film and Video Festival in New York City on 27 October 2009, where it won Best International Feature Film – Arthouse Genre.
Melancholie der Engel: It was later screened at BUT( B- Movies, Underground, and Trash) Film Festival in the Netherlands on 7 June 2013.
Melancholie der Engel: The DVD was released on 30 July 2010 in Austria.
Melancholie der Engel: The film received largely negative reviews.
Melancholie der Engel: While some commended the cinematography, it was seen to be an exploitative hardcore film with repetitive and meaningless depravity communicating its nihilistic message.
The Time, the Place and the Girl (1946 film): The Time, the Place and the Girl is a 1946 American musical film directed by David Butler.
The Time, the Place and the Girl (1946 film): It is unrelated to the 1929 film" The Time, the Place and the Girl".
Edith Meinhard: Edith Meinhard is a German retired actress who appeared in more than fifty films during her career including the 1929 film" Diary of a Lost Girl".
Matt Corboy: Matt Corboy( born June 4, 1973) is an American actor.
Matt Corboy: He has appeared in both films and television series.
Illusion (1929 film): Illusion is a 1929 American Pre-Code drama film directed by Lothar Mendes and written by Richard H. Digges Jr., E. Lloyd Sheldon and Arthur Chesney Train.
Illusion (1929 film): The film stars Charles' Buddy' Rogers, Nancy Carroll, June Collyer, Kay Francis, Regis Toomey, Knute Erickson and Eugenie Besserer.
Illusion (1929 film): The film was released on September 21, 1929, by Paramount Pictures.

Marian Dora: Marian Dora( born 1970 in Southern Germany) is the pseudonym most commonly used by an anonymous German director, cinematographer, actor, screenwriter, editor, producer, composer, assistant director, makeup artist, special effects/ sound/ camera/ electricity technician, and set decorator/ designer, anagram of his actual name, occasionally also credited under several other pseudonyms including Marian Dora Bolutino, Marian Dora Botulino, Marian D. Bolutino, M.D. Botulino, Marian D. Botulino, Art Doran, M.D. Bolutino, A. Doran, and Marian Dallamano.
Jack Shea (director): Jack Shea (August 1, 1928 – April 28, 2013) was an American film and television director.
Jack Shea (director): He was the president of the Directors Guild of America from 1997 to 2002.
E. Pierce Marshall: Everett Pierce Marshall (January 12, 1939 – June 20, 2006) was an American petroleum industry executive.
E. Pierce Marshall: He was the beneficial owner of 16% of Koch Industries, which he received as an inheritance from his father, J. Howard Marshall II.

E. Pierce Marshall: He spent the last 15 years of his life as a defendant in lawsuits by his stepmother, Anna Nicole Smith, and his brother, J. Howard Marshall III, who both sought part of his father's fortune after being left out of the will and testament.
Hypatius (consul 359): Flavius Hypatius( c. 340- died after AD 383) was a Roman Senator, who was the brother- in- law of the Roman emperor Constantius II.
Robert Vadra: Robert Vadra is an Indian businessman, entrepreneur and the husband of Priyanka Gandhi.
Robert Vadra: He is the son -in- law of Sonia Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, and the brother- in- law of Rahul Gandhi.
Wyndham Goold: Wyndham Goold( 1812-1854) was a Member of Parliament( MP) for County Limerick from 1850 to 1854.
Wyndham Goold: Goold was educated at Westminster School and Trinity College, Dublin.
Wyndham Goold: He was the son in law of Frederick Falkiner Goold, Archdeacon of Raphoe and brother in law of Bishop Hamilton Verschoyle
Robert W. Levering: Robert Woodrow Levering( October 3, 1914 – August 11, 1989) was a U.S. Representative from Ohio, son-in- law of Usher L. Burdick and brother- in- law of Quentin N. Burdick.
Nick Sidi: Nick Sidi( born 22 February 1966 in Manchester, England) is an English actor.
Nick Sidi: He is the son -in- law of actress Rosalind Knight and brother- in- law of actress Susannah Elliott- Knight.
Nick Sidi: He often plays drama or comedy roles on television and frequently appears in BBC dramas.
Elaine Tettemer Marshall: Elaine Tettemer Marshall (born July 22, 1942) is an American billionaire as a result of an inheritance.

Elaine Tettemer Marshall: Trusts for the benefit of Marshall and her sons own the 16% beneficial interest in Koch Industries; formerly owned by her husband, E. Pierce Marshall, to whom she was married from 1965 until his death in 2006.
Elaine Tettemer Marshall: These shares were previously owned by her father in-law, J. Howard Marshall, who was married to Anna Nicole Smith in the last year of his life.
Elaine Tettemer Marshall: Elaine has been a member of the board of directors of Koch Industries since the 2006 death of her husband.
Eusebius (consul 359): Flavius Eusebius( died after AD 371) was a Roman Senator, who was the brother- in- law of the emperor Constantius II.
Charles Francis Norton: Charles Francis Norton( 1807 – 1835) was a 19th- century Member of Parliament for Guildford.
Charles Francis Norton: Norton was also a Captain of 52nd Light Infantry; son-in- law of Sir Colin Campbell; brother- in- law of writer Caroline Norton
Greg Penner: Gregory B. Penner( born December 18, 1969) is an American businessman and venture capitalist.
Greg Penner: Penner was named the chairman of Walmart on June 5, 2015.
Greg Penner: He is the son-in- law of S. Robson Walton and the grandson- in- law of Sam Walton, the founder of Walmart.
Eunoë (wife of Bogudes): Eunoë was the wife of Bogudes, King of Mauretania.
Lloyd Corrigan: Lloyd Corrigan (October 16, 1900 – November 5, 1969) was an American film and television actor, producer, screenwriter, and director who began working in films in the 1920s.
Lloyd Corrigan: The son of actress Lillian Elliott, Corrigan directed films,

Lloyd Corrigan: usually mysteries such as "Daughter of the Dragon" starring Anna May Wong (one of a trilogy of Fu Manchu movies for which he has writing credits), before dedicating himself more to acting in 1938.
Lloyd Corrigan: His short "La Cucaracha" won an Academy Award in 1935.
Catherine Exley: Catherine Exley was the wife of a soldier and accompanied her husband when he served in Portugal, Spain and Ireland during the Napoleonic Wars.
Catherine Exley: She is best known as the author of a diary that gives an account of military life in that era from the viewpoint of the wife of a common soldier.
James Corrigan: James Corrigan (17 October 1867 – 28 February 1929), was an American actor.
James Corrigan: He appeared in 16 films between 1920 and 1927.
James Corrigan: He was born in Ohio, United States and died in Los Angeles, California.
James Corrigan: Corrigan was the father of actor Lloyd Corrigan.
Artaynte: Artaynte( f. 478 BC), was the wife of the Crown Prince Darius.
Empress Shōken: , also known as, was the wife of Emperor Meiji of Japan.
Agatha (wife of Samuel of Bulgaria): Agatha was the wife of Emperor Samuel of Bulgaria.
Lillie Connolly: Lillie Connolly" née" Reynolds( 1867- 1938) was the wife of James Connolly, the Irish revolutionary who was involved in the 1916 Easter Rising.
Hafsa Hatun: Hafsa Hatun was the wife of Sultan Bayezid I of the Ottoman Empire.
Éléonore Desmier d'Olbreuse: Éléonore Marie Desmier d'Olbreuse (3 January 1639 – 5 February 1722) was the wife of George William, Duke of Lauenburg and Prince of Celle.
Éléonore Desmier d'Olbreuse: She was the mother of Sophia Dorothea of Celle, who was the wife of George I of Great Britain.
Éléonore Desmier d'Olbreuse: Thus she is the maternal grandmother of George II.
